title: ShipBoard
problem_statement: Engineering teams operating 5–50 microservices lack a unified deployment health dashboard, forcing engineering managers to spend 30–60 minutes per week manually aggregating deploy frequency, rollback rate, and lead time metrics from siloed tools like GitHub Actions, Jenkins, and ArgoCD. When cascading rollbacks occur, identifying the originating service requires manual log correlation across three or more systems with no shared timeline. This fragmentation increases in cost and risk as microservice counts grow and leadership expectations for real-time reliability data intensify. ShipBoard addresses this by providing a single correlated pane of glass for deployment health across all CI/CD integrations.
target_users: Engineering manager overseeing 5–50 microservices who prepares weekly reliability reports for leadership
On-call platform engineer who investigates and resolves cascading deployment failures across multiple services
VP of Engineering or CTO who needs real-time deployment reliability data for executive reviews
DevOps engineer responsible for configuring and maintaining CI/CD pipelines across GitHub Actions, Jenkins, and ArgoCD
Staff software engineer who monitors the deployment health of services they own
user_stories: As an engineering manager overseeing 5–50 microservices who prepares weekly reliability reports for leadership, I want a single dashboard showing deploy frequency, rollback rate, and lead time aggregated across all connected CI/CD tools so that I can generate my weekly reliability report in under 5 minutes without switching between systems

As an on-call platform engineer who investigates and resolves cascading deployment failures across multiple services, I want a correlated deployment timeline that highlights the first service to roll back and surfaces all downstream rollbacks triggered within a configurable time window so that I can identify the root-cause service in under 10 minutes without manual log spelunking

As a VP of Engineering or CTO who needs real-time deployment reliability data for executive reviews, I want an auto-generated reliability summary showing DORA metrics trends over the past 30 and 90 days so that I can answer leadership questions about deployment health without waiting for manual reports from my engineering managers

As a DevOps engineer responsible for configuring and maintaining CI/CD pipelines across GitHub Actions, Jenkins, and ArgoCD, I want a guided integration wizard for each supported CI/CD tool that validates connectivity and normalizes webhook payloads so that I can onboard a new tool integration in under 30 minutes with no custom scripting

As a staff software engineer who monitors the deployment health of services they own, I want per-service deployment health cards showing current deploy status, recent rollback history, and mean lead time so that I can proactively identify degrading trends in my services before they escalate to incidents

As an engineering manager overseeing 5–50 microservices who prepares weekly reliability reports for leadership, I want configurable alerting thresholds that notify me via Slack or email when a service's rollback rate exceeds a defined percentage over a rolling 7-day window so that I can intervene before reliability issues surface in leadership reviews

As an on-call platform engineer who investigates and resolves cascading deployment failures across multiple services, I want a filterable event log that correlates deployment events across all services on a single timeline with source-tool attribution so that I can reconstruct the exact sequence of events during an incident without accessing three separate systems
acceptance_criteria: The unified dashboard displays deploy frequency, rollback rate, and lead time for all connected services updated within 60 seconds of a deployment event being received

The correlated rollback timeline correctly identifies the first rolling-back service and all downstream rollbacks occurring within a user-configurable window (default 30 minutes) with at least 95% accuracy in a test scenario involving 10 or more services

Integration wizards for GitHub Actions, Jenkins, and ArgoCD each complete end-to-end connectivity validation and begin ingesting normalized deployment events within 30 minutes of starting setup, requiring zero custom scripting from the user

Each DORA metric (deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate, mean time to restore) is calculated correctly as validated against a known reference dataset with less than 1% variance
Per-service deployment health cards render current deploy status, last 10 rollback events, and 30-day mean lead time with data no older than 2 minutes under normal operating conditions
Slack and email alerts for rollback rate threshold breaches are delivered within 5 minutes of the threshold being crossed, configurable per service and per team
The auto-generated reliability summary report can be exported as a PDF or shared via a unique URL, and contains 30-day and 90-day trend charts for all four DORA metrics
The system supports ingestion of at least 10,000 deployment events per hour per tenant without degrading dashboard load time beyond 3 seconds at p95
Role-based access control allows engineering managers to grant read-only dashboard access to VP/CTO personas without exposing raw pipeline configuration or credentials
All data in transit and at rest is encrypted using AES-256 and TLS 1.2 or higher, verified by a third-party security scan prior to GA release

success_metrics.metric: Time engineering managers spend manually compiling weekly reliability reports
success_metrics.target: Under 5 minutes per week per manager within 90 days of adoption

success_metrics.metric: Mean time to identify root-cause service during a cascading rollback incident
success_metrics.baseline: 45–90 minutes requiring log access across 3+ systems (self-reported)
success_metrics.target: Under 10 minutes using ShipBoard correlated timeline within 60 days of adoption

success_metrics.metric: Percentage of connected CI/CD integrations completed without engineering support tickets
success_metrics.baseline: 0% (no existing integration wizard; all integrations require custom scripting)
success_metrics.target: 85% or more of new integrations completed self-serve within 30 minutes

success_metrics.metric: Weekly active usage rate among engineering managers at accounts with 3+ connected services
success_metrics.target: 70% or more of engineering manager seats active weekly at 6 months post-launch

success_metrics.metric: Customer-reported DORA metric data accuracy versus source-of-truth CI/CD tool logs
success_metrics.baseline: Not measured (metrics currently compiled manually with no validation)
success_metrics.target: 99% or greater accuracy as measured by quarterly automated reconciliation against raw pipeline logs

risks_open_questions: API rate limits on GitHub Actions, Jenkins, and ArgoCD may delay event ingestion during high-volume deployment periods — need to define queueing and backpressure strategy before beta
Customers with self-hosted Jenkins or ArgoCD instances behind firewalls will require an agent-based ingestion model; scope and timeline for a self-hosted agent are not yet defined

Defining 'rollback' consistently across CI/CD tools is non-trivial — GitHub Actions redeployments, ArgoCD sync reversions, and Jenkins build retries have different semantics; normalization logic must be validated with at least 5 design partners before GA

Multi-cloud and hybrid deployment environments (e.g., services deployed to both EKS and GKE) may produce duplicate or out-of-order events that corrupt lead time calculations — deduplication strategy must be designed and tested

Privacy and compliance requirements vary by enterprise customer; some customers may prohibit sending deployment metadata to a SaaS platform — need to assess demand for an on-premises or VPC-hosted deployment option
How should ShipBoard handle services that use blue/green or canary deployments where a 'rollback' is ambiguous — partial traffic shift reversal vs. full rollback?
What is the minimum viable integration surface for Jenkins given the breadth of its plugin ecosystem — which plugins will be supported at launch and which will be deferred?
Pricing model is undecided: per-seat, per-service, or per-event volume — each creates different incentives and may conflict with enterprise procurement norms
Will ShipBoard store raw log data or only normalized deployment events? Storing raw logs increases storage cost and compliance surface area significantly
Is there sufficient demand for a mobile view of the reliability dashboard for on-call engineers, or is desktop-first sufficient for the initial release?
out_of_scope: Execution or triggering of deployments — ShipBoard is read-only and observability-only; it does not orchestrate or modify pipelines
Log aggregation, distributed tracing, or APM functionality — ShipBoard ingests deployment events only, not application runtime logs or traces
Incident management workflows such as paging, escalation policies, or postmortem templates — these remain in tools like PagerDuty or Jira
Support for non-deployment CI pipeline stages such as unit test results, code coverage, or static analysis metrics
Cost analytics for cloud infrastructure or CI/CD compute spend
Code review or pull request analytics beyond lead time as it relates to deployment events
Built-in remediation or automated rollback triggering based on detected anomalies
Support for mobile native applications (iOS/Android) in the initial release
Integration with ticketing systems such as Jira or ServiceNow in v1
Multi-tenancy features such as org-level hierarchies or business-unit-level billing in v1
